summary.intent: Push the speed-optimization commits for the Caliper checker (perf/checker-extract-speed) to the remote with --no-verify, while a follow-up worker builds perf/checker-shared-bases.
summary.outcome: The speed commits were not pushed: the first attempt used the wrong local branch and was rejected as non-fast-forward, and the corrected retry was blocked by the permission classifier. The Entire stop hook panicked at every turn end, and the user was given a corrected `! git push --no-verify origin 4c59ef11:refs/heads/perf/checker-extract-speed` command to run themselves.

repo: The speed commits live at 4c59ef11 (3 commits: tests, docs+changeset, lint fixes); the remote perf/checker-extract-speed is at 854da4c6.
The local branch worktree-agent-aed2d7748791ef6ec points at main's tip (8212aef8), not the speed commits, so pushing by branch name fails as non-fast-forward. Push by SHA instead.
The repo has extensions.worktreeconfig=true, 461 branch.* config entries, core.ignorecase=true, and a core.hookspath pointing at another project's .moon/hooks.
Entire is installed as Homebrew cask entire@nightly 0.13.4-nightly.202611121940.
Benchmark results from the speed worker: gate-large 7.25s (RDT) vs 1.82s (Caliper), about 4.0x faster; Chakra-only 4.10s vs 1.37s, about 3.0x faster.

code.finding: readFoldsCase calls Section on a nil *config.Config (go-git v6 beta), causing a SIGSEGV. The call chain is foldsCase (298) -> StoredRef (242) -> resolveLocalRef (184) -> resolveRefMaybeFetch (629) -> refBaseForBackfill (379) -> backfillTranscript (532). It hits any command that writes or reads checkpoint refs: the push hook, the stop hook and `checkpoint list`.

workflow: The permission classifier blocks `git push --no-verify` as an auto-mode bypass even with chat authorization, and then blocked follow-up read-only git commands. The user must run it via `! <command>` in the prompt.
Push by explicit SHA (`git push origin <sha>:refs/heads/<name>`) rather than by a worktree branch name. Git's non-fast-forward rejection protects against overwriting the remote.
Give a worker a SHA rather than a branch name as its base, and verify the worker's base when it reports.
--no-verify skips Entire's checkpoint sync, so run `entire checkpoint list --outgoing` after Entire is fixed to see whether session logs still need pushing.

friction: The Entire stop hook panics with a nil-pointer dereference at the end of every turn, repeating the same trace more than ten times and adding noise.
The permission classifier denied the push even with the user's explicit go-ahead, and also denied later read-only git diagnostics, which blocked checking the follow-up worker's state.
The first push used the wrong local branch (main's tip), which was rejected as a non-fast-forward.
The root cause of the Entire panic is unconfirmed. It is a hypothesis that extensions.worktreeConfig or a missing .git/config.worktree yields a nil config, and it could not be tested.
The follow-up worker may have been briefed with the wrong base, since the branch name pointed at main's tip rather than the speed head.
open_items: The user needs to run the corrected push: `! cd /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper && git push --no-verify origin 4c59ef11:refs/heads/perf/checker-extract-speed`.
Test the Entire hypothesis: check for .git/config.worktree, touch it if missing, re-run `entire checkpoint list --outgoing`, then try `entire doctor` and a rollback of the cask.
Consider reporting to the Entire team that readFoldsCase dereferences a nil config, possibly when extensions.worktreeConfig=true.
Check the follow-up worker's (perf/checker-shared-bases) base commit when it reports, and verify its measurements and diffs are against the speed head 4c59ef11.
Push the follow-up worker's commits too, once its branch tip is known.
After Entire is fixed, run `entire checkpoint list --outgoing` to find session logs skipped by --no-verify.
